panels.title: Session Timers
panels.description: Session lifetime timers, ONE stat panel with three tiles SIDE-BY-SIDE (orientation=vertical => columns). LAST ACK = seconds since the main loop last acked ANY claude-event (time() - claude_mainloop_last_ack_timestamp_seconds; green<360, amber>=360, red>=600). That is the whole liveness story: the loop runs `event-ack ack-batch` after every event batch it handles, which stamps last-ack-timestamp, and `claude-watch metrics` exports it. A wedged loop stops acking and this climbs. CLAUDE UPTIME = seconds since the Claude Code process started (claude_process_start_timestamp_seconds, derived from /proc so it renders on a bare host AND in a container). SINCE CLEAR = seconds since the context was last RESET -- a /clear (daemon auto-clear, self-clear, or hand-typed) or a compaction, all of which throw the context away and rebuild it (n/a if none recorded). The daemon stamps it on the check cycle where it OBSERVES the reset, so the value trails the actual reset by at most one check_interval; it recognises a reset from a below-30K token sample OR a halved token counter, the latter because a fresh context on a big-preamble session boots well above 30K and would otherwise never be seen (2026-08-22: a 907979 -> 77185 clear went unrecorded and this tile read 1.07 days 50 minutes after the clear). There used to be a fourth tile, LAST ACK AGE, fed by the age of a marker claude-event-watch wrote each time it surfaced a heartbeat-tick. It and the HEARTBEAT tile (the heartbeat FILE's mtime) were two approximations of the same question, and the marker lived inside the event queue dir where a health-check counted it as an unconsumed event and fired false WATCHER DOWN alerts. Both are retired (2026-08-22); this single tile measures the quantity directly. No value => the loop has never acked, rendered as "n/a" (kept short: the old tile's explanatory n/a string overflowed at every width).

panels.title: Tokens / Minute (excl. cache reads)
panels.description: Tokens per minute, averaged over 1m / 5m / 15m. claude_code_tokens_total is a cumulative COUNTER, so each tile is rate(...[window]) * 60 — never the raw counter. type="cache_read" is excluded: cache reads re-count the whole cached prefix on every request and dominate the sum by ~300x, which would make the tiles read in the millions rather than the actual burn rate.

panels.title: Build Info
panels.description:
What is running and what shipped last. Left two tiles come from the claude_watch_build_info gauge the daemon's textfile collector writes (src/metrics.rs): the commit the RUNNING binary was built from, and the PR that commit came in on. They describe the deployed binary, so they only move on a deploy.

The third tile does that same job for the work-queue-exporter, which ships as its own container image on its own schedule and so can be a different revision from the daemon: worktask_exporter_build_info carries the commit baked in at image build (--build-arg CW_BUILD_COMMIT, the same host-resolves-it-and-passes-it-in mechanism the daemon's gauge uses, because .dockerignore prunes .git from the build context) or supplied at runtime via $WORKTASK_EXPORTER_COMMIT. commit=unknown there means the build args never reached the image; an EMPTY tile means the deployed exporter predates the metric. See monitoring/prometheus/README.md.

The fourth tile is the repo's side of the same question -- the most recently MERGED pull request on GitHub -- and it moves the moment a PR merges, which is what makes the pair useful: a gap between them is un-deployed work. It is read directly from GitHub by the Infinity datasource (uid `infinity`, backend parser), NOT from Prometheus, which is why this panel's datasource is `-- Mixed --`. There is deliberately no exporter behind it: a local exporter scraping GitHub for one number is one more service to run, restart and forget, and the value it holds is already public.

RANKING IS BY merged_at, NOT BY PR NUMBER. The JSONata root selector `$[merged_at != null]^(>merged_at)[0]` drops the closed-but-never-merged PRs, sorts what is left by merge time descending and takes the first. Number order inverts merged order routinely -- two PRs open at once merge in whichever order goes green first (#680 merged after #681 on 2026-08-22) -- so `max(number)` would show the wrong PR every time that happens. The URL's sort=updated is only a cheap way to get recent PRs into the first page; a comment or a label bumps updated_at without merging anything, so the ordering that matters is redone here.

UNAUTHENTICATED, and that is the constraint on how often it may run. GitHub allows 60 requests/hour/IP without a token, and one dashboard refresh with this panel on screen is one request -- Grafana has no per-panel refresh interval, so the call rate is the DASHBOARD refresh rate whenever this panel is in the viewport (panels scrolled out of view are not queried). That is why this dashboard's refresh is 5m (2026-08-22): at the 30s it previously shipped, a viewport parked here burned the hour's budget in 30 minutes, GitHub answered 403, and the tile showed a query error until the window rolled — and the panel's 5m min interval does not change that, because Infinity ignores it. 5m puts the worst case at 12/hour and costs this board nothing, since nothing here needs sub-minute freshness and every alerting decision is made by Prometheus rules rather than by a rendered panel. A deployment that wants sub-minute refresh back should give the Infinity datasource a GitHub token (5,000/hour) first. Rate-limited or offline, the failure is confined to this tile and its error marker -- the three Prometheus tiles keep rendering.

Where the Infinity datasource is not provisioned this tile simply does not appear (Grafana flags the missing datasource on the panel; the three Prometheus tiles still render). Infinity is not part of a default Grafana install: see monitoring/dashboards/README.md for the plugin install and the uid `infinity` provisioning stanza it needs.

panels.title: Output Tokens (by model, period)
panels.description: Cumulative OUTPUT tokens by model over the dashboard's time range (increase() of the windowed claude_output_tokens_total gauge; Andrew #5370 — tokens = cumulative OUTPUT, split by model).

panels.title: Ack Staleness
panels.description: Seconds since the main loop last acked ANY claude-event, over time. The stat tile above shows the current value; this shows whether it is a spike or a trend. Renamed from "Heartbeat Staleness" 2026-08-22 when the host heartbeat file was retired in favour of the ack timestamp.

panels.title: Reminder Fires by Type (rate / 5m)
panels.description: Rate of hook-driven reminder fires. context_high fires when context % crosses the high threshold; version_update fires when a new claude version is detected; pre_compact fires before a compaction.

panels.title: Fallback Injections by Type (rate / 5m)
panels.description: Rate of daemon-driven fallback injections. When nonzero, Claude ignored the corresponding reminder and the daemon had to intervene (force /clear or /restart).

panels.title: Cooperation Ratio (30m)
panels.description: Fraction of context_high reminders that Claude acted on autonomously (did NOT require fallback). Computed as 1 - (fallback clear rate / context_high reminder rate) over 30m. Target >= 0.8. Falls back to 1.0 when no reminders fired in the window.

panels.title: Reminder→Action Latency (avg)
panels.description: Average time from reminder fire to Claude action (self-/clear or /restart), split by type. Computed as sum/count since the exporter ships counter pairs rather than a true histogram -- this is an AVERAGE, not a real quantile. Samples only when Claude acted within 1h (context) / 6h (version).

panels.title: Counter Values (debug)
panels.description: Raw counter values for debugging: reminder_fires and fallback_injections by type, plus latency sum/count pairs.

panels.title: Total Interrupts (24h)
panels.description: Sum of all claude_interrupts_total increases across every kind over the last 24h. Red above 50 (wedge-state territory), yellow above 20.

panels.title: Interrupts per Kind (1h)
panels.description: Per-kind count of interrupts fired in the last hour. Quick triage to spot which kind is currently firing.

panels.title: Interrupts by Kind (rate / min)
panels.description: Per-minute rate of claude_interrupts_total by kind, smoothed over 5m. Stacked area. Key chart for noise monitoring and cascade detection.

panels.title: Cascade Indicator (10m avg /min)
panels.description: Total interrupts per minute averaged over 10m. Red > 2/min indicates cascade state (like yesterday's wedge).

panels.title: Tokens This Month (MTD)
panels.description: Total Claude Code token usage for the current calendar month. Sums input + output + cache_creation + cache_read across all retained transcripts whose timestamp falls in this month. Resets on the 1st.

panels.title: Token Usage by Day
panels.description: Rolling 24h token usage stacked by type. With only partial-day data the bars show today's running total; once multi-day data accumulates the chart shows the rolling 24h window as a time series. Bars are stacked input/output/cache_creation/cache_read.

panels.title: Tool Calls (by tool)
panels.description: Fleet-wide tool calls, by tool name (claude_tool_use_total) — a windowed gauge folded over every live/recent transcript, not a monotonic counter.

panels.title: Agents Spawned
panels.description: Distinct Claude Code subagent transcripts observed in the live/recent window (claude_agent_spawned_count) — a windowed gauge, not a lifetime total.
